title: Compact-support base change at finite coefficients
statement:
Let $f:X\to Y$ be separated of finite type and admit a compactification $c=(j,p)$, with $j:X\hookrightarrow\overline X$ a quasi-compact open immersion and $p:\overline X\to Y$ proper. Let $\Lambda$ be a finite commutative ring and $g:Y'\to Y$ any morphism. Form the cartesian compact-support square [def-cbc-compact-support-square] with projections $g':X'=X\times_Y Y'\to X$ and $f':X'\to Y'$, and the base-changed compactification $c'=(j',p')$. For every complex $K\in D^+(X_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], the exchange map of [def-cbc-exchange-map]
$$\operatorname{Ex}_!^c(K):g^{-1}Rf_!^cK\longrightarrow Rf'_!^{c'}g'^{-1}K$$
is an isomorphism in $D^+(Y'_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$, where $Rf_!^c=Rp_*j_!$ [def-weil-pbc-projection-compactification]. The maps agree under the canonical comparisons obtained from the proper/open refinement maps [def-weil-pbc-proper-open-comparison], independently of $c$ and of the common refinement used to compare compactifications [lem-cbc-compactifiable-cofiltered]. Consequently they define the compactification-independent map $\operatorname{Ex}_!:g^{-1}Rf_!K\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf'_!g'^{-1}K$. They are natural in $K$, are identities for identity base changes, and satisfy horizontal and vertical pasting after inserting the canonical inverse-image associativity and compact-support composition isomorphisms. Vertical pasting is asserted for composable compact-support squares (so compactifications of both morphisms and their composite are supplied); composition is computed using the compatible towers of [lem-cbc-compactifiable-compatible-tower]. No hypothesis on $g$ or on residue characteristics, no constructibility, and no qcqs hypothesis on the base schemes is required.

proof.text: Use the supplied compactification $c=(j,p)$. [lem-cbc-compactifiable-cofiltered] gives its base-changed compactification and refinements under arbitrary $g$. The upper open square is cartesian by the fibre-product construction in [def-cbc-compact-support-square]. Write $M=j_!K$. Exactness in [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-exact] allows degreewise $j_!$ to descend to $D^+$; a representative zero below a fixed degree stays zero there. By [def-cbc-exchange-map], the map to prove invertible is exactly $(Rp'_*\beta_K)\circ\operatorname{Ex}^{\Lambda}_{*,p}(M)$, with $\beta:\bar g'^{-1}j_!\cong j'_!g'^{-1}$.

source.place: Tag 0F7I, construction before lemma-shriek-well-defined; blueprint proof first displayed composite

proof.text: The additive group of finite $\Lambda$ has finite exponent: for each $a\in\Lambda$ two nonnegative multiples coincide, so a positive integer kills $a$; multiplying these integers over all elements gives $N>0$ with $N\Lambda=0$. Then $N1_\Lambda=0$, so $Nx=(N1_\Lambda)x=0$ for every element of every $\Lambda$-module. Thus the underlying abelian cohomology sheaves of $M$ are torsion. Apply [thm-weil-pbc-bounded-below] to the proper $p$, its cartesian square and the bounded-below underlying abelian complex. Its exchange is invertible. The exact forgetful comparison [lem-weil-pbc-exchange-forget-coefficients] identifies this map with the underlying map of the specific module exchange in step 1 and reflects invertibility. Hence $\operatorname{Ex}^{\Lambda}_{*,p}(M)$ is invertible. No prime invertibility or constructibility is used.

source.place: Tag 0DDE, label lemma-proper-base-change (bounded-below complexes with torsion cohomology), deduced from Tag 095T, label theorem-proper-base-change; applied to the proper factor as in the blueprint

proof.text: Apply [cor-cbc-derived-extension-zero-base-change] to the upper open square from step 1. It gives precisely the invertible $\beta_K$ in [def-cbc-exchange-map]. Applying $Rp'_*$ preserves its inverse (the image of $\beta_K^{-1}$). Therefore the composite in step 1 has inverse $\operatorname{Ex}_{*,p}^{-1}\circ Rp'_*(\beta_K^{-1})$, which proves invertibility. Both factors are natural transformations: the proper exchange is the unit/counit composite specified in the definition and $\beta$ is natural by the cited corollary. Their composite is consequently natural in $K$.

source.place: Tag 03S6, label lemma-shriek-base-change (abelian sheaves and module sheaves); blueprint proof first paragraph

proof.text:
For a refinement $u:c_1\to c_2$ write $p_1=p_2u$ and let $u'$ be its base change. By [def-weil-pbc-proper-open-comparison], $\alpha_u:j_{2!}\to Ru_*j_{1!}$ is the refinement comparison; [lem-cbc-proper-open-interchange-coherence] identifies it with $\gamma$ for the square with left vertical identity, right vertical $u$, and opens $j_1,j_2$. Put $C_u=Rp_{2,*}\alpha_u:F_{c_2}\to F_{c_1}$, inserting direct-image composition. The base-change equation for $\gamma$ reads
$$ Ru'_*\beta_1\circ\operatorname{Ex}_{*,u}(j_{1!})\circ\bar g_2^{-1}\alpha_u
=\alpha_{u'}g'^{-1}\circ\beta_2.$$
Apply $Rp'_{2,*}$ and precede by $\operatorname{Ex}_{*,p_2}(j_{2!})$. Naturality moves $\alpha_u$ past this latter exchange. The vertical proper-exchange equation [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting], applied directly to the module-coefficient adjunctions in [def-cbc-exchange-map], identifies the two successive proper exchanges for $p_2,u$ with the exchange for $p_1$. This yields the explicit comparison square
$$ C_{u'}g'^{-1}\circ\operatorname{Ex}_!^{c_2}=\operatorname{Ex}_!^{c_1}\circ g^{-1}C_u.$$
Thus a refinement comparison intertwines the compact-support exchange maps, rather than merely comparing their objects.

The comparison maps $\alpha_u$ are invertible by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-open-comparison-iso] and obey $\alpha_{vu}=(Rv_*\alpha_u)\alpha_v$, $\alpha_{\mathrm{id}}=\mathrm{id}$ by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-open-comparison-composition]. Derived direct-image composition [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition] then gives $C_{vu}=C_uC_v$ and $C_{\mathrm{id}}=\mathrm{id}$: expand $Rp_{3,*}Rv_*Ru_*$, replace $(Rv_*\alpha_u)\alpha_v$ by $\alpha_{vu}$, and use naturality to move the composition identifications past the comparison. To check the associativity normalization choose a bounded-below injective representative $I$ using [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-enough-injectives] and [lem-weil-pbc-dplus-injective-representative]. Every successive direct image of $I$ is still bounded below and injective by [lem-weil-pbc-direct-image-preserves-injectives], hence K-injective by the representative lemma. In the normalization of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition] each further resolution may be the identity. Both associativity composites are therefore the underived identification $(pvu)_*I=p_*v_*u_*I$, whose equality is evaluation on the same etale test object and the unique projection-preserving associativity isomorphism of fibre products [def-pc-fibre-product], [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. Naturality extends the equality to every derived object. For $c,d$ choose a common refinement $e\xrightarrow{r}c$, $e\xrightarrow{s}d$ by [lem-cbc-compactifiable-cofiltered], and put $I_{c,d}=C_s^{-1}C_r$. Refining $e$ by $t$ leaves this ratio unchanged since $(C_tC_s)^{-1}(C_tC_r)=C_s^{-1}C_r$. For another common refinement $e'$ first find a common refinement of $e,e'$, then equalize its two arrows to $c$ and its two arrows to $d$, using the equalizer clause of that same cofilteredness node. The ratios there agree, hence the original ratios agree. A common refinement of three compactifications gives $I_{d,k}I_{c,d}=I_{c,k}$ by cancellation. Apply the equation of step 4 to $r,s$ and cancel $C_{s'}$ to obtain
$$I_{c',d'}g'^{-1}\circ\operatorname{Ex}_!^c=\operatorname{Ex}_!^d\circ g^{-1}I_{c,d}.$$
This constructs the canonical ordinary etale comparisons and proves independence of the exchange; no pro-etale comparison is used.

source.place: Tag 0F7I, lemma-shriek-well-defined; cancellation in the blueprint refinement paragraph

proof.text: For an identity base change, [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting] makes the proper factor the identity after inserting the unit isomorphisms; [cor-cbc-derived-extension-zero-base-change] makes $\beta$ the identity too. Their composite is the identity. For two successive base changes $g,h$, compute all compactifications by base-changing $c$. Expand the two composite maps as the four factors $h^{-1}\operatorname{Ex}_{*,p}$, $h^{-1}Rp'_*\beta_g$, $\operatorname{Ex}_{*,p'}$ and $Rp''_*\beta_h$. Naturality of $\operatorname{Ex}_{*,p'}$ moves $\beta_g$ through it. The proper horizontal pasting equation combines the two proper factors, and the open horizontal pasting equation combines $h^{-1}\beta_g$ and $\beta_h$. The result is exactly the two-factor formula of [def-cbc-exchange-map] for $gh$. These equations are proved directly for modules using [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting], not inferred from faithfulness of derived forgetting: the latter is not assumed. Inverse-image composition is termwise pullback along composite maps; both associativity maps preserve every fibre-product projection, so their square isomorphisms paste. The unit/counit mate formula is explicitly the module formula of [def-cbc-exchange-map]. Apply clauses (1), (2), (4) of the generic mate theorem to these pasted or identity inverse-image squares to obtain respectively the horizontal, vertical and identity proper-exchange equations. The direct-image composition is normalized as in step 5. For each change of compactification, the comparison square of step 5 conjugates both sides by the same invertible comparisons; cancellation proves the equation for those choices.

source.place: Tag 07A7, label remark-base-change (mate construction); labels remark-compose-base-change and remark-compose-base-change-horizontal (pasting formulas); their omitted verifications are supplied by the cited Mathlib mate-pasting node; blueprint final sentence

proof.text:
For vertically pasted squares with $X\xrightarrow{f}Y\xrightarrow{h}Z$, use [lem-cbc-compactifiable-compatible-tower] to choose $Y\xrightarrow{i}\bar Y\xrightarrow{q}Z$, $X\xrightarrow{a}\bar X\xrightarrow{p}\bar Y$, and $U=\bar X\times_{\bar Y}Y$, with opens $c:X\to U$, $b:U\to\bar X$, $a=bc$, and proper $p_Y:U\to Y$. These choices and their base changes compute $Rf_!=Rp_{Y,*}c_!$, $Rh_!=Rq_*i_!$ and $R(hf)_!=R(qp)_*a_!$. The composition isomorphism of the compatible-tower composition construction is the chain
$$Rq_*i_!Rp_{Y,*}c_!\xrightarrow{Rq_*\gamma\,c_!}Rq_*Rp_*b_!c_!\cong R(qp)_*a_!.$$
Here $\gamma$ is the open/proper square with horizontal opens $b,i$ and vertical maps $p_Y,p$. Expand the two compact-support exchanges for $h,f$. Apply the base-change equation for $\gamma$ in [lem-cbc-proper-open-interchange-coherence] to commute this chain through the pullback: its two sides identify the $i_!Rp_{Y,*}$ portion before and after base change. The remaining successive proper factors for $q,p$ combine by the vertical equation [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting]. The two open factors for $b,c$ combine by the pasting equation [cor-cbc-derived-extension-zero-base-change]. This leaves precisely $\operatorname{Ex}_{*,qp}(a_!K)$ followed by the extension-by-zero comparison for $a$, which is the exchange for $hf$. The common refining tower asserted by [lem-cbc-compactifiable-compatible-tower] reduces comparison of any two towers to tower refinements. For clarity, let tower 1 refine tower 2 by proper maps $w:U_1\to U_2$, $v:\bar X_1\to\bar X_2$, $u:\bar Y_1\to\bar Y_2$. Denote the refinement comparisons by $\gamma_A:c_{2!}\to Rw_*c_{1!}$, $\gamma_D:i_{2!}\to Ru_*i_{1!}$ and $\gamma_E:a_{2!}\to Rv_*a_{1!}$. Let $\gamma_F:b_{2!}Rw_*\to Rv_*b_{1!}$ correspond to $vb_1=b_2w$, and let $\gamma_\nu:i_{\nu!}Rp_{Y,\nu,*}\to Rp_{\nu,*}b_{\nu!}$ correspond to tower $\nu$. All vertical maps are proper, including $w$ by the common-tower statement. Horizontal interchange composition gives $\gamma_E=(\gamma_F c_{1!})\circ(b_{2!}\gamma_A)$. The two vertical pastings of the square $U_1\to\bar X_1$ over $Y\to\bar Y_2$ give
$$ (Rp_{2,*}\gamma_F)\circ(\gamma_2 Rw_*)=(Ru_*\gamma_1)\circ(\gamma_D Rp_{Y,1,*}), $$
after identifying $Rp_{2,*}Rv_*=Ru_*Rp_{1,*}$ and $Rp_{Y,2,*}Rw_*=Rp_{Y,1,*}$. Compose with $i_{2!}Rp_{Y,2,*}\gamma_A$ and apply $Rq_{2,*}$. Naturality moves $\gamma_A$ through $\gamma_2$; the horizontal equation replaces $(\gamma_F c_{1!})\circ(b_{2!}\gamma_A)$ by $\gamma_E$. The result is
$$ C_{hf}\circ\mu_2=\mu_1\circ(C_h Rf_!^{1})\circ(Rh_!^{2}C_f), $$
where $C_f=Rp_{Y,2,*}\gamma_A$, $C_h=Rq_{2,*}\gamma_D$ and $C_{hf}=R(q_2p_2)_*\gamma_E$, inserting the direct-image composition isomorphisms. Apply this equation to the common refining tower and each original tower. Step 5 cancels its invertible comparisons, proving independence of the composition chain from all choices. Thus, writing $\mu:Rh_!Rf_!\cong R(hf)_!$, the asserted equation is
$$\operatorname{Ex}_{!,hf}\circ g^{-1}\mu=\mu' g_X^{-1}\circ(Rh'_!\operatorname{Ex}_{!,f})\circ(\operatorname{Ex}_{!,h}Rf_!).$$
All proper maps and opens come from the cited compatible tower, and the coefficient category stays ordinary etale throughout. The open composition $b_!c_!\cong a_!$ used here follows from [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-adjunction]: maps from $b_!c_!F$ to $H$ correspond successively to maps from $c_!F$ to $b^{-1}H$, then from $F$ to $c^{-1}b^{-1}H=a^{-1}H$, hence from $a_!F$ to $H$. These natural Hom bijections give the canonical isomorphism, whose degreewise derived version exists by [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-exact]. Its identity and associativity follow because both iterated Hom bijections are restriction to the same open subset.
